quests.instruction: Your friend gets a shiny new bike and you still have your old one. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Wanting something nice that someone else just got can give you a tight, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Wanting something nice that someone else just got can give you a tight, wanting feeling inside.
quests.funFact: Cheering for a friend's good news, even with this feeling, is a kind and grown-up thing to practice.

quests.instruction: You wait all year for the town fair, but it is cancelled this year. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Missing out on something you looked forward to all year can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Missing out on something you looked forward to for a long time can leave you feeling let down.
quests.funFact: Fairs come back every year — this year's wait just means an even more special one next time!

quests.instruction: You trip and fall in front of the whole cafeteria. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Having everyone notice a little accident can make your cheeks turn warm and pink.
quests.explanation: Having everyone notice a small accident can make your cheeks feel warm and a little shy.
quests.funFact: A quick laugh at yourself is a great way to shrink this warm, shy feeling fast!

quests.instruction: Your grandpa spends the whole afternoon teaching you how to fish. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Someone spending their whole afternoon just to teach you something new can feel very warm.
quests.explanation: Someone spending their whole afternoon teaching you something new fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Learning a skill from someone you love is a memory that often lasts a lifetime!

quests.instruction: You are waiting for your turn to give a book report. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting for your turn to speak in front of the class can make your hands feel a little shaky.
quests.explanation: Waiting for your turn to speak in front of others can give you a shaky, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Practicing your report out loud at home can help this feeling feel much smaller.

quests.instruction: Someone keeps cutting ahead of you at the water fountain. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: Waiting your turn while others keep skipping ahead does not feel fair.
quests.explanation: Waiting your turn while others keep skipping ahead feels very unfair and frustrating.
quests.funFact: Politely reminding someone about the line often solves this kind of mix-up quickly.

quests.instruction: Your tablet battery dies in the middle of a long car trip. How do you feel?
quests.question: Bored
quests.hint: Losing your favorite way to pass the time on a long trip can feel very slow.
quests.explanation: Losing your favorite way to pass the time on a long trip can make it feel slow and dull.
quests.funFact: Simple games like counting license plate colors can make a car trip fun again!

quests.instruction: You just finished playing in a whole soccer tournament in one day. How do you feel?
quests.question: Tired
quests.hint: A full day of running and playing many games can leave your legs feeling heavy.
quests.explanation: A full day of running and playing many games can leave your whole body feeling worn out.
quests.funFact: Drinking water and resting after a big tournament helps your muscles recover faster!

quests.instruction: Your grandparents leave after a fun, long visit. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Saying goodbye to someone you love after a fun visit can bring a heavy feeling.
quests.explanation: Saying goodbye to someone you love after a fun visit can bring on a quiet, heavy feeling.
quests.funFact: Planning the next visit together is a nice way to look forward to seeing them again!

quests.instruction: You have to ask the librarian for help finding a book. How do you feel?
quests.question: Shy
quests.hint: Talking to someone you do not know well can make you want to speak softly.
quests.explanation: Talking to someone you do not know very well can make you feel a little quiet and unsure.
quests.funFact: Librarians love helping kids find books — asking is easier than it feels!

quests.instruction: Your friend gets a gaming console you have wanted for a long time. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Watching a friend get something you have wished for can give you a tight, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Watching a friend get something you have wished for can give you a tight, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking to play together is a great way to enjoy the new thing without needing to own it too!

quests.instruction: You practice all week for the game, but it gets rained out. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Having something you prepared hard for get cancelled can leave your shoulders low.
quests.explanation: Having something you prepared hard for get cancelled can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Games that get rained out are almost always rescheduled for another day!

quests.instruction: You realize you have spinach stuck in your teeth after lunch. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Noticing something silly on your face that others may have seen can make your cheeks feel warm.
quests.explanation: Noticing something silly others may have seen can make your cheeks feel warm and shy.
quests.funFact: Checking a mirror quickly is a simple way to fix this and feel better right away!

quests.instruction: Your coach gives up part of their lunch break to help you practice. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Someone using their own free time to help you improve can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Someone giving up their free time to help you improve fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Coaches often say watching a player improve is one of the best parts of their job!

quests.instruction: You are about to ask your teacher a question in front of the whole class. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Speaking up in front of everyone can make your voice feel a little shaky.
quests.explanation: Speaking up in front of a group can give you a shaky, fluttery feeling right before you talk.
quests.funFact: Teachers love questions — asking one usually helps this fluttery feeling disappear fast!

quests.instruction: Your friend blames you for a mess you did not make. How do you feel?
quests.question: Angry
quests.hint: Getting blamed for something unfair can make your face feel hot.
quests.explanation: Getting blamed for something you did not do feels very unfair and frustrating.
quests.funFact: Calmly explaining what really happened is the best way to solve a mix-up like this.

quests.instruction: You are stuck inside during a long holiday weekend with nothing new to do. How do you feel?
quests.question: Bored
quests.hint: A long stretch of days with nothing new planned can feel slow.
quests.explanation: A long stretch of days with nothing new to do can make the time feel slow and dull.
quests.funFact: A simple scavenger hunt around the house can turn a dull day into a fun one!

quests.instruction: You wake up extra early for a family trip. How do you feel?
quests.question: Tired
quests.hint: Waking up before your body is ready can make your eyes feel heavy.
quests.explanation: Waking up earlier than your body is used to can make you feel worn out and sleepy.
quests.funFact: A short nap in the car can help your body catch up on the missing rest!

quests.instruction: You lose your favorite hat on a windy day at the beach. How do you feel?
quests.question: Sad
quests.hint: Watching something you love blow away can bring a little frown.
quests.explanation: Losing something you love on a windy day can bring on a quiet, disappointed feeling.
quests.funFact: A hat with a chin strap can help keep favorites from blowing away next time!

quests.instruction: A new student sits next to you and you are not sure what to say. How do you feel?
quests.question: Shy
quests.hint: Not knowing how to start a conversation with someone new can make you feel quiet.
quests.explanation: Not knowing how to start a conversation with someone new can make you feel quiet and unsure.
quests.funFact: Asking 'what's your name?' is one of the easiest ways to start any new friendship!

quests.instruction: Your sibling gets a bigger slice of cake than you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Noticing someone else got a little more than you can give you an unfair, wanting feeling.
quests.explanation: Noticing someone else got a little more than you can give you a small, wanting feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking calmly to have things measured evenly can help solve moments like this fairly.

quests.instruction: You do not get invited to a party that most of your friends are going to. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Being left out of plans your friends are excited about can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Being left out of plans your friends are excited about can leave you with a heavy, letdown feeling.
quests.funFact: Planning your own fun activity for that day can help turn this feeling around.

quests.instruction: You forget your line during the school play in front of everyone. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Blanking on your words in front of a full audience can make your face feel warm.
quests.explanation: Forgetting your line in front of an audience can make your cheeks feel warm and shy.
quests.funFact: Even professional actors forget their lines sometimes — helpers off-stage are ready to help!

quests.instruction: Your friend shares their umbrella with you in the rain. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Staying dry because a friend thought of you can make your heart feel warm.
quests.explanation: Staying dry because a friend thought to share fills you with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Sharing something as simple as an umbrella is a small act that builds strong friendships!

quests.instruction: You are getting ready to try out for the soccer team. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting to show your skills in front of a coach can make your stomach flutter.
quests.explanation: Waiting to show your skills in a tryout can give you a fluttery feeling right beforehand.
quests.funFact: Even professional athletes say they still feel this way before a big tryout or game!

quests.instruction: Your classmate gets picked for the lead role you wanted in the play. How do you feel?
quests.question: Jealous
quests.hint: Missing out on something you wanted while someone else gets it can feel tight and uncomfortable.
quests.explanation: Missing out on something you really wanted, while someone else gets it, can give you an uncomfortable feeling.
quests.funFact: Supporting your classmate while still trying your best next time shows real teamwork spirit!

quests.instruction: Your art project does not turn out the way you pictured it in your head. How do you feel?
quests.question: Disappointed
quests.hint: Working hard on something that does not turn out as planned can leave you feeling let down.
quests.explanation: Working hard on something that does not turn out as planned can leave you feeling a little let down.
quests.funFact: Many famous artists say their first try rarely matches the picture in their head — that is normal!

quests.instruction: Your voice cracks in the middle of your class presentation. How do you feel?
quests.question: Embarrassed
quests.hint: Having your voice do something unexpected in front of the class can make you feel warm and shy.
quests.explanation: Having your voice crack in front of the class can make your cheeks feel warm and shy.
quests.funFact: Voice cracks happen to everyone sometimes and are simply part of how voices work and grow!

quests.instruction: Your parents surprise you with your favorite meal after a long day. How do you feel?
quests.question: Thankful
quests.hint: Coming home to a favorite treat someone made just for you can fill your heart with warmth.
quests.explanation: Coming home to a favorite meal made just for you fills your heart with a warm, grateful feeling.
quests.funFact: Saying thank you for small everyday kindnesses helps families feel closer to each other!

quests.instruction: You are getting ready to perform in the school talent show. How do you feel?
quests.question: Nervous
quests.hint: Waiting backstage before showing off a skill to a big crowd can feel shaky.
quests.explanation: Waiting backstage before a big performance can give you a shaky, fluttery feeling.
quests.funFact: Taking a few slow breaths backstage is a trick many performers use to feel steadier.
